requirements.text:
clamp(x, lo, hi) reads its arguments as signed integers. It returns lo when x < lo, else hi
when x > hi, else x.
requirements.reason: The claim uses signed 32-bit comparisons and returns lo, hi, or x in exactly the order specified. It covers every input combination.

requirements.text:
gcd(a, b) reads its arguments as unsigned integers and returns their greatest common divisor,
with gcd(a, 0) = a.
requirements.reason: The claim computes the unsigned inputs’ greatest common divisor for every pair. In particular, the standard natural-number gcd gives gcd(a, 0) = a, including gcd(0, 0) = 0.

requirements.text: sum_to(n) reads n as an unsigned integer and returns 0 + 1 + ... + (n - 1), wrapped to 32 bits.
requirements.reason: The claim sums the natural numbers below the unsigned input and encodes the result as a 32-bit value, which wraps modulo 2³² as required.

claims.summary: The exported sum_to function returns the 32-bit wrapping sum of the natural numbers below its input.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit input, interpreted as an unsigned natural number.
Returns the sum of all natural numbers below the input, encoded in 32 bits; the result wraps modulo 2³².
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and that the call terminates without trapping under every host behavior.

claims.summary: The exported clamp function returns one of its inputs according to signed 32-bit comparisons.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent:
`clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` if `x < lo`, else `hi` if `x > hi`, else `x`
(tested in this order, so with `lo > hi` the result is `lo` for `x < lo` and `hi` otherwise).
details: Covers every combination of three 32-bit inputs, each interpreted as a signed two’s-complement integer for comparison.

Returns the lower bound when the first input is below it; otherwise returns the upper bound when that bound is below the first input; otherwise returns the first input. The selected 32-bit value is returned unchanged, with no arithmetic wraparound.
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and that the call terminates without trapping under every host behavior.
caveats: If the lower bound is greater than the upper bound, the claim still specifies the nested signed comparisons; it does not guarantee a conventional clamp into a valid interval.
The elaborated comparisons are signed 32-bit comparisons, regardless of whether the source-level inputs might be mistaken for unsigned values.

claims.summary: The exported gcd function returns the greatest common divisor of the unsigned values of its two inputs.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, each converted to an unsigned natural number before computing the greatest common divisor.
Returns that greatest common divisor encoded in 32 bits; the result fits in the input width, so the encoding does not change it through wraparound.
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and that the call terminates without trapping under every host behavior.
caveats: The inputs are treated as unsigned bit-pattern values, not as signed integers; this can differ from a signed greatest-common-divisor interpretation for values with the high bit set.
